To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the N-termini of TIMPs can be engineered to selectively inhibit individual members of the ADAMTS family of proteases.

N-terminal reactive-site mutants of TIMP-1 (tissue inhibitor metalloproteinases-1) and TIMP-3 have different affinities for ADAM17 (ADAM with disintegrin and a metalloproteinase domain) and ADAMTS (a disintegrins and metalloproteinases with thrombospondins) and can be used to selectively inhibit these metalloproteinase families.
N-TIMP- 3(T2G) and [−1A], [−2A], [−3A]N-TIMPs are potent and selective inhibitors of ADAMTS- 4 and ADAMTs-5.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the structural determinants of the selectivity of N-TIMP for ADAM17, and the design of N-TIMP mutants with enhanced inhibitory activity against ADAM17, which may prove to be useful therapeutic agents in the treatment of diseases involving inflammation, arthritis and cancer.
the development of novel, potent, selective and stable inhibitors of ADAMs and MMPs.

developing inhibitors of ADAMTS-1-5 and ADAM17 that are selective for these metalloproteinase families over the MMPs, which may be useful in the treatment of diseases associated with excessive matrix metalloproteinase activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
N-TIMP-2 and N-TIMP-1, and their mutants, are more potent inhibitors of the ADAMTSs than N-TIMP-4 and N-TIMP3.
the N-termini of TIMPs are important for their interactions with ADAMs and MMPs.
the N-TIMP-1 mutants [−1A], [−2A], [−3A] and [−4A] are selective for MMP-9 and MMP-13, whereas the [−1G]N-TIMP, N-TIMP-2 and [−1A, −2A]N- TIMP-2 are selective for MMP2 and MMP-9.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

N-TIMP-4, -5 and -3 are the best inhibitors for ADAMTSs, MMP-9 and -2 respectively, whereas [−2A]-TIMP-2, [−3A]-TIMP1, [−1A]-TIMP3 and [−1A, −2A]TIMP3 are the best for ADAM17, MMP-7, ADAMTSs and MMP-1 respectively.
the reactive-site mutants [−1A], [−2A], [−1A][−1G], [−2G][−1G] and [−2G] are all selective inhibitors of ADAM17 and ADAMTSs.

N-TIMP-4, N-TIMP-5 and N-TIMP-6, which have the same N-termini as N-TIMP-1, N-TIMP 2 and N-TIMP3, respectively, are likely to have similar inhibitory specificities to the latter three TIMPs, but with the added advantage of having a longer N-terminus which may allow further discrimination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reactive site of TIMP-1 is the most conserved among all TIMPs, and that TIMP-1 can be used to inhibit all ADAMs and MMPs.
the TIMP-3 inhibitory domain (N-TIMP- 3) is a good starting point for the development of selective inhibitors of ADAMTSs, and that the reactive site is a key target for such inhibitors.
TIMPs can be modified to inhibit a subset of the metalloproteinases and that these modified inhibitors may have potential therapeutic value.
